title: My Stepdaughter Sold My Machines, Sent a Spool Check. So I Let Her Stitch Her Docket Number
description: I invested my late husband's $118,000 nursing pension into restoring rare antique sewing machines with my stepdaughter, only for her to forge a dissolution and sell them for $720,000, mailing me a $4,200 'spool' check. When I found the original notarized partnership agreement folded inside a 130-year-old Willcox & Gibbs bobbin case, the museum sale collapsed and she now stitches quilt labels bearing her perjury docket number in a prison smock. #Betrayal #RevengeStory #AntiqueSewingMachines
thumb_text: SHE STITCHES QUILT LABELS WITH HER PERJURY DOCKET NUMBER
pinned_comment: If your stepdaughter forged a dissolution to sell your late husband's antique sewing machines for $720K and mailed you a $4,200 spool check, would you have let her end up stitching perjury labels in a prison smock? Share your story in the comments.
